newsitem.title: UK: Standard P&I Club to open Singapore subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Standard P&I Club to open Singapore subsidiary.

text.p: Mutual marine insurer The Standard P&I (protection and indemnity) Club said in a statement on Thursday that it will set up a subsidiary in Singapore.
Standard Asia will be an authorised Singapore insurance company and will provide insurance to shipowners from the Asia Pacific region, it said.
The Standard is the first P&I club to set up in Singapore and said it expects to become a force in the region within five years.

The announcement, which confirms recent local press reports, comes the day after the Asian Shipowners Forum called for the development of a local insurance industry and the Singapore insurance commissioner said the country aimed to become a focus for Asian marine insurance.
Singapore is in talks with at least one other P&I club, the UK club, with a view to setting up an operation in the country.
A spokesman for the UK Club told Reuters it hoped the Singapore authorities would announce their decision soon on its application.
The Bermuda based Standard insures 34 million gross tons of shipping.
It belongs to the international group of P&I clubs which buy insurance for their shipowner members. Between them they insure 95 percent of all ocean-going ships.
Asian shipowners control over 169 million gross tons, or around 40 percent of the world total.
